Bulgarian Electric Utilities Targeted as Protesters Block Key Sites Amid Political Dispute

SOFIA, Bulgaria, June 11—Electric utilities across Bulgaria are facing significant disruption after groups of protesters occupied and blockaded several critical power generation and distribution sites on Tuesday, in what the government has described as a politically motivated action. The protest, which began in the early hours of the morning, has affected facilities operated by Bulgarian Energy Holding EAD and other major providers.

The demonstrators, numbering in the hundreds, say they are demanding changes to national energy policy and transparency in the management of public utilities. At least four major substations and a hydroelectric plant have been rendered inoperable as a result of the blockades, according to the Bulgarian Association of Electric Utility Operators.

"These actions have already led to temporary power fluctuations and forced load reductions in several regions," said Ivaylo Petrov, spokesperson for Bulgarian Energy Holding EAD. "Our priority is to ensure the safety of our staff and the stability of the power grid while we work with authorities to restore normal operations."

According to preliminary estimates from the National Electric Grid Union, roughly 18% of Bulgaria’s electricity generation capacity is currently offline or restricted due to the ongoing occupation. Grid operators have begun implementing contingency plans to prevent wider outages, including importing electricity from neighboring countries.

Energy analyst Mariya Stoycheva warned that extended disruptions could have "serious consequences for supply reliability and long-term infrastructure investment." Unions representing utility workers have called for urgent mediation, stating in a joint release, "We urge all parties to find a peaceful and swift resolution to prevent further damage to Bulgaria’s electric system."

Authorities are continuing negotiations with protest leaders as of Tuesday evening.
